name: Roflumilast cream
lead: Roflumilast cream (brand name Zoryve, developed by Arcutis) is a topical phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE-4) inhibitor. The US FDA approved the 0.3% cream for plaque psoriasis in July 2022, a 0.3% foam for seborrheic dermatitis in December 2023, and a 0.15% cream for atopic dermatitis in July 2024.[1] Seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis and eczema are visible skin conditions, which is the basis of its appearance relevance.

By dampening the inflammatory signalling behind red, scaly and itchy patches, a prescription non-steroid cream can leave the skin of the face, scalp, hands and body looking calmer and clearer. Trials measure this with investigator ratings of how clear or almost clear the skin is, along with itch scores.[2][3][8]
Phase 3 trials have tested it in plaque psoriasis and atopic dermatitis.[2][3] Other uses such as vitiligo have not been the subject of reported trials.

paras: Approved uses in the US are plaque psoriasis (age 12 and over), seborrheic dermatitis (foam, age 9 and over) and mild to moderate atopic dermatitis (age 6 and over for the 0.15% cream, with a 0.05% cream extended to ages 2 to 5 in October 2025).[1] The foam also received a plaque psoriasis approval for adults and adolescents 12 and over in May 2025.[1]

Because psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis commonly involve the scalp, hairline, face and skin folds, and eczema often shows on the face and hands, the visible clearing of these areas is the practical benefit patients describe in trials as skin that is clear or almost clear.[2][3]

The cream is not a cosmetic and is prescribed for diagnosed inflammatory skin disease. Its appearance effect comes from treating that disease: plaques flatten, redness fades and flaking lessens as inflammation settles. One registered study examined it in facial papulopustular rosacea, a condition with visible redness and bumps on the face.[9]
Unlike topical corticosteroids, it is a non-steroid, a point often raised in discussions of treating thin facial skin and skin folds over longer periods.

Roflumilast is a selective, long-acting PDE-4 inhibitor with anti-inflammatory effects.[1] PDE-4 breaks down cyclic AMP inside inflammatory cells, so blocking it raises cAMP and reduces release of inflammatory messengers.[1] Pharmacokinetic data from phase 1 to 3 psoriasis studies have been published.[4]

The same molecule was first developed as an oral tablet for severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, approved in the EU in 2010 and the US in 2011, and is associated with Takeda, AstraZeneca and AbbVie; the topical forms were developed by Arcutis.[1] It is also available as a generic oral medicine.[1]

The oral tablet is associated with diarrhea, weight loss, nausea, headache, insomnia, decreased appetite and depression.[1] Topical-specific adverse events are reported in the trial publications and product label rather than in general references.[2][3] In the INTEGUMENT-PED trial of children aged 2 to 5, safety and local tolerability were assessed alongside efficacy.[8]
Roflumilast is prescription-only in the US, UK, Canada, Australia and the EU.[1]

A phase 2b trial in plaque psoriasis tested 0.3% and 0.15% cream against vehicle for 12 weeks,[5] and the DERMIS-1 and DERMIS-2 phase 3 trials (about 440 participants each) tested 0.3% cream for 8 weeks.[2] A 52-week open-label study of 332 adults reported long-term safety and effectiveness, with 73.5 percent completing.[6]

In atopic dermatitis, phase 2 and the INTEGUMENT-1 and -2 phase 3 trials tested 0.15% cream against vehicle once daily for 4 weeks in patients aged 6 and over, with success defined as clear or almost clear skin plus at least a two-grade improvement.[3][7] INTEGUMENT-PED studied the 0.05% cream in children aged 2 to 5; among 437 roflumilast and 215 vehicle patients, 25.4 percent versus 10.7 percent reached that success level at week 4.[8] Registered studies include facial papulopustular rosacea (n=40).[9] No trial for vitiligo has been reported.

card.summary: A prescription PDE-4 inhibitor cream and foam approved for psoriasis, eczema and scalp or facial seborrheic dermatitis, with phase 3 data for psoriasis and eczema.

quick.overview:
Roflumilast cream (Zoryve) is a steroid-free topical approved in the US for plaque psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis (foam) and atopic dermatitis.
Phase 3 randomized trials support the psoriasis and eczema uses; off-label talk about vitiligo has no trials behind it in the sources found.
quick.mechanism: It selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase-4, an enzyme involved in inflammatory signaling in skin.
quick.risks: Prescription only. Topical adverse events are reported in trial publications and the label; oral roflumilast tablets list diarrhea, nausea, headache and insomnia.

chain: Topical PDE-4 inhibition raises cAMP and lowers inflammatory signalling
Less redness, scale and itch in affected skin
Visibly clearer skin on face, scalp and body
angle.text: Dermatologists prescribe roflumilast cream or foam to calm inflammatory skin conditions that show on the face, scalp and body. In trials the main goal was skin rated clear or almost clear, which is how treated skin looks to an observer.
